why: The student treats the println after 'if (x > 0);' as the if's body, but the ';' is an empty statement that is the whole body, so the answer uses a wrong rule and says positive is not printed when the run shows it is.

concepts.quote: positive is not printed, because x > 0 is false.
concepts.why: The student reads the ';' as just ending the line and misses that it forms the then-branch, which is the SemicolonAfterIfHeader error, so the println always runs.

concepts.quote: positive is not printed, because x > 0 is false.
concepts.why: The student reads the if as the English 'if x is positive, do the next line' and picks the wrong body, so the predicted output contradicts how Java runs it.
With x = -3, x > 0 does give false, so this one comparison is right.
The answer says nothing about assignment.
